newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia likely to sell 97 pct of Rosneft Oil.
newsitem.headline: Russia likely to sell 97 pct of Rosneft Oil.

text.p: Russia is likely to sell off 97 percent of the Rosneft oil company, including a 51 percent stake in September, a senior Rosneft official said on Tuesday.

Alexander Belov, first deputy head of the company's privatisation and securities department, said Rosneft's board had agreed the plan at a meeting late on Monday and that parts of the sales would be open to foreign investors.
Belov also said Rosneft Board Chairman Alexander Putilov may seek approval to scrap a law limiting foreign ownership in oil companies to 15 percent in order win wider foreign investment.

He said Rosneft's board had approved proposals by property authorities and the Fuel and Energy Ministry to scrap a company clause saying 51 percent of the company had to remain state property for three years.
Rosneft is the last major Russian oil company to be privatised and is valued for, among other things, its status as the state's agent in production-sharing deals.
